## Notes

**Quick read:** Early creator (joined Jun 28) who films faceless, aesthetic text-overlay clips of her toddler boy on her back and hip at home and at a tropical zoo, including a dad clip; 4 of 4 approved and in ads with a healthy ROAS of 1.61, but only 4 videos in three months.
**Best next move:** answer her Sep 22 "if you have any ideas of something you specifically would like to see I'm always open!" with concrete ideas this week; it is unanswered.

### Style (from watching her videos)
- On camera: dark-haired mom, glasses sometimes, braid, casual (striped linen shirt, green floral shorts). Toddler boy about 12 to 18 months in a yellow outfit; her husband appears in the zoo clips; a grey pit bull is in the kitchen. Setting: a bright white modern home with tiled floors (feels like Florida) and a tropical zoo boardwalk.
- Format: text-only, no talking, mostly filmed from behind or at a distance, music-driven, 8 to 13 seconds. Hooks: "The Bambora carrier is so comfortable and convenient", "Even dads want to use it", "Everything I got to do today thanks to my Bambora Sling Carrier" ending "have an amazing, productive, and cry free day with my boy". The Aug 28 video is a real day-in-the-life ("This was our legitimate day yesterday. Just filmed everything I actually did!").
- What worked: all 4 approved and run as ads; 18a50732 (text version of the hallway plus zoo dad clip) ran in 2 ads. 48 purchases, $2,751 purchase value on $1,713 spend. The three Jul 28 videos are the same footage with different or no text (0f1b5afb has no overlay).
- Safety and checklist: brown sling, toddler sits in the seat with legs out on the back-hip carry. Issue in d3182022 (Aug 28): a chores montage ("vacuum", "organize") where she crouches on the floor sorting shoes with both hands and vacuums with the toddler on, which reads as hands free and doing chores while wearing. The dad zoo shots are from behind so his supporting hand is only partly visible. Buckle and safety loop are never shown up close.
- Strengths: clean aesthetic, feels real and aspirational, the dad angle is rare on the roster, very short edits that suit Meta placements.
- To improve: keep a hand on him in chore scenes (or film calmer moments like walks and cuddles); add one close shot of the buckle and seat; more volume.
